annotation.authors_or_issuer: Reczka, K.; Zalewska, Z.; Szymkowiak, J.; Woźniak, M.
key_provisions_or_claims: Perceived usefulness, fear of the unknown and trust are the main psychological determinants of adoption.
Robots may reduce loneliness but risk displacing authentic human interaction.
Key ethical concerns: privacy, data security, dehumanization, objectification and informed consent for cognitively impaired patients.
Algorithmic bias may exclude vulnerable older patients.
Design must be user-centered, balancing empathy with ethical risk minimization.
annotation.summary_en: Narrative review of literature on socio-psychological determinants of older adults' acceptance of AI-driven social assistive robots in geriatric care, and associated ethical challenges including privacy, dehumanization, consent, and algorithmic bias. Concludes that user-centered, empathetic design is needed to build trust and minimize ethical risk.
annotation.title_clean: Socio-Psychological Determinants of Adopting AI-Driven Robotic Assistants in Geriatric Care: A Review of Current Trends and Ethical Challenges
